subject: Unplugged Sequencing & Algorithms
arc_note: Grade 1 · Ontario Math C3 (Coding), UNPLUGGED — an algorithm is a set of steps carried out in order to do a job. NO on-screen blocks (that is the separate G1 Block Coding subject), NO loops, NO concurrency. Lane = ordered STEP-CARDS: each step is a short DECODABLE phrase on a labelled card (A/B/C/D), and the child orders / follows / writes / reasons about the order. ≤6 steps; light decodable reading + simple shapes (the `symbols` primitive supplies number/order cards). Distinct from the Block-Coding subject (number-path program) and from the next subject Intro Debugging (which is dedicated sequence REPAIR) — here the focus is reading, following, and WRITING algorithms (C3.1) plus describing how order affects the result (C3.2), not fixing broken ones. Several tasks are mathematical situations (make an AB pattern, build a tower, count a set) for strong C3/C1 alignment; the rest are familiar routines (plant a seed, get ready, make toast). Each correct order / dependency / validity is MODELLED + asserted in solution.py (canonical order + precedence checks). I/we/you-do scaffold + a predict/think-first prompt on every sheet; the teacher answer key explains WHY the order works and what breaks if reordered. Cite C3.1 + C3.2 verbatim from the Grade-1 cache.
